affected_nodes.original_theorem:
ASTIS-authored bounded heterogeneous binary probability-product background independently sealed before proof.
For arbitrary measurable spaces X,Y and actual probability laws mu,nu, let F be jointly measurable, nonnegative at every point, and bounded above by some real constant. Define Phi(t)=t log t, A(x)=integral F(x,y) dnu, B(y)=integral F(x,y) dmu, and m=integral F d(mu product nu). The actual joint function and its Phi transform are integrable, every fixed-coordinate slice and its Phi transform are integrable, and both actual marginals and their Phi transforms are integrable. The sum of the two marginal Phi integrals is at most the joint Phi integral plus Phi(m). Zero mass and zero fibers are included.
Exact scope: Genuine bounded nonnegative measurable functions on arbitrary probability product; true joint/all-slice/marginal L1 and marginal entropy inequality including zero fibers/mass. Bounded class sufficient for actual compact C2 squared-function consumer; not an unrestricted unbounded SLT theorem, finite tensorization, Gaussian Hilbert/cutoffLSI, T2/FIRST/main/cost.
theorem bounded_product_entropy_subadditivity
    {X Y : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y]
    (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (F : X × Y → ℝ) (hF : Measurable F)
    (hF0 : ∀ z, 0 ≤ F z) (hFb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ z, F z ≤ C) :
    let Φ : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => t * Real.log t
    let A : X → ℝ := fun x => ∫ y, F (x, y) ∂ν
    let B : Y → ℝ := fun y => ∫ x, F (x, y) ∂μ
    let m : ℝ := ∫ z, F z ∂μ.prod ν
    Integrable F (μ.prod ν) ∧
    Integrable (fun z => Φ (F z)) (μ.prod ν) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun y => F (x, y)) ν ∧
      Integrable (fun y => Φ (F (x, y))) ν) ∧
    (∀ y, Integrable (fun x => F (x, y)) μ ∧
      Integrable (fun x => Φ (F (x, y))) μ) ∧
    Integrable A μ ∧ Integrable B ν ∧
    Integrable (fun x => Φ (A x)) μ ∧ Integrable (fun y => Φ (B y)) ν ∧
    (∫ x, Φ (A x) ∂μ) + (∫ y, Φ (B y) ∂ν) ≤
      (∫ z, Φ (F z) ∂μ.prod ν) + Φ m

affected_nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let X and Y be arbitrary measurable spaces, and let mu and nu be probability measures on X and Y, respectively. Give X x Y its product measurable structure and the actual product measure mu x nu. Let F : X x Y -> R be measurable. Suppose F(x,y) >= 0 for every (x,y), and suppose there exists a real C such that F(x,y) <= C for every (x,y).

Define Phi(t) = t log(t) using the totalized real logarithm; in particular log(0) = 0 and Phi(0) = 0. Define the actual slice integrals A(x) = integral_Y F(x,y) dnu(y), B(y) = integral_X F(x,y) dmu(x), and the actual product integral m = integral_(X x Y) F(x,y) d(mu x nu)(x,y). Every integral here and below is a real Bochner integral.

Then F and Phi composed with F are Bochner integrable under mu x nu. For every x in X, both y |-> F(x,y) and y |-> Phi(F(x,y)) are Bochner integrable under nu. For every y in Y, both x |-> F(x,y) and x |-> Phi(F(x,y)) are Bochner integrable under mu. A and Phi composed with A are Bochner integrable under mu, and B and Phi composed with B are Bochner integrable under nu. Moreover,

integral_X Phi(A(x)) dmu(x) + integral_Y Phi(B(y)) dnu(y)
    <= integral_(X x Y) Phi(F(x,y)) d(mu x nu)(x,y) + Phi(m).

The integrability assertions and this inequality form one conjunctive conclusion. Every slice assertion holds for all points in the corresponding parameter space, not merely almost everywhere. There is no strictly positive lower bound on F or positive-mass assumption on m. The zero case uses the displayed totalized Phi directly, without a separate normalization or division by m.
